items.title: FEMA denies Illinois disaster declaration after August storms, state to appeal
items.summary: The Federal Emergency Management Agency rejected Illinois' request for a major disaster declaration in a letter dated Oct 7, saying federal assistance was not warranted. The denial covers Champaign, Cook, Ford, Fulton, McLean, Tazewell, Vermilion and Will counties, including Chicago neighborhoods in the 34th Ward. Governor JB Pritzker announced the state will appeal the decision, citing extensive damage to homes, infrastructure, flooding and power outages. The denial comes as President Donald Trump has also been refusing disaster aid to Illinois while approving aid for other states.

items.title: Governor Pritzker launches bipartisan PJM Governors' Collaborative to curb electricity costs
items.summary: At the Governors' Summit on the State of PJM held at the Palmer House Hilton, Governor JB Pritzker announced a new bipartisan PJM Governors' Collaborative formalized through a memorandum of understanding with governors from nine other PJM states. The collaborative aims to give states a stronger voice in decisions by PJM, the regional transmission organization that manages the electric grid for parts of 13 states. Pritzker highlighted concerns about high electricity prices and the impact of data centers on consumer utility bills. The initiative is part of his broader effort to keep energy reliable and affordable for Illinois residents.

items.title: Chicago inspector general pushes for AI use in city government
items.summary: Newly appointed Chicago inspector general David Glockner said city agencies tend to lag on technology and urged the city to deploy artificial intelligence to improve efficiency for taxpayers. Glockner suggested that Chicago has barely scratched the surface of AI applications and that broader adoption could benefit city services. The call comes as city leaders consider modernizing operations and could affect how local services are delivered in neighborhoods such as the West Loop and South Loop.

items.title: Billionaire accused of feeding rats
items.summary: The city is weighing legal action against Lincoln Park billionaire Barre Seid over claims that his nut-spreading operation is fueling a rat infestation around Green City Market, Ald. Timmy Knudsen (43rd) says. The infestation is causing property damage that could leave taxpayers on the hook for repairs, according to city documents.

items.title: Abbott 5K and Chicago Marathon bring extensive street closures to the 34th Ward
items.summary: The Abbott 5K will start at 6:30 am on Saturday, October 10, with parking bans beginning at 1 am, and streets in the Loop will be closed to traffic until 9:30 am. The Bank of America Chicago Marathon will cause additional closures throughout the 34th Ward on Sunday, October 11, with all closures beginning at 6 am and parking restrictions starting at 1 am. Cheering stations will be at Mary Bartelme Park starting at 8 am on Sunday, and residents are advised to keep garbage carts accessible Tuesday‑Friday to avoid ticketing and towing.

items.title: Green and Pink Line service interruptions from October 13‑26 due to Lake Street Bridge replacement
items.summary: CTA will interrupt Green and Pink Line service between Clinton and the Clark/Lake stations beginning at 4 am on October 13 and ending at 4 am on October 26 while the Lake Street Bridge is rebuilt. Green Line riders will use free bus substitutions between Clinton and Clark/Lake, and Pink Line riders will transfer to the Blue Line at Racine for downtown service. Milwaukee Street will be closed from Canal to Fulton between October 5 and October 30.

items.title: Loop Arts Fest scheduled for October 17 on State Street
items.summary: The Loop Arts Fest will run from 12 pm to 6 pm on October 17 along State Street between Madison and Jackson, featuring three blocks of programming, two stages of live entertainment and a headliner. The event will showcase arts and culture organizations, local artists, food vendors and Chicago businesses. Attendees can explore a variety of performances and installations throughout the festival.

items.title: West Loop Tower Bringing First Aldi Breaks Ground
items.summary: The West Loop Tower development has begun construction of the first Aldi store in the neighborhood, marking a major retail addition to the West Loop. The new store will serve local residents and businesses, adding convenience and competition to the area. The project is part of the larger West Loop Tower mixed‑use development.

items.title: Morgan & Ashland CTA Service Suspended Oct. 13-26
items.summary: CTA will suspend service on the Morgan & Ashland line from October 13 to 26, affecting commuters in the West Loop and surrounding neighborhoods. Riders will need to use alternate routes or modes of transportation during the suspension. The service interruption is scheduled to allow for maintenance or upgrades.

items.title: Black Briar Ribbon Cutting at 201 N. Morgan St.
items.summary: Black Briar, a new restaurant led by Chef Jimmy Papadopoulos and co‑owner Tim Anderson, opened its Fulton Market location at 201 N. Morgan St. after a ribbon‑cutting ceremony. The menu features fresh seafood, house‑made pastas, steaks, and inventive cocktails. The opening adds to Fulton Market’s vibrant dining scene.

items.title: CTA workers call for more safety after janitor killed at Green Line station on Near West Side
items.summary: Transit workers are demanding answers after a CTA employee was stabbed and killed during a confrontation at a Green Line station.

items.title: CTA janitor fatally stabbed at Green Line train station on Near West Side, officials say
items.summary: Union leaders are remembering a CTA rail janitor as a hero after he was fatally stabbed at a Green Line train station Thursday on Chicago's Near West Side.

items.title: Chicago Aldermen Want More Power To Crack Down On ‘Problem Bars’
items.summary: The proposal would strengthen licensing enforcement, require faster compliance with corrective plans and give the city more leverage to close businesses tied to repeated violence or nuisance complaints.

items.title: Here Are Road Closures, Parking Restrictions For Chicago Marathon Weekend
items.summary: Major streets around Grant Park will close as early as 4 a.m. Sunday. Additional closures have already begun and will continue throughout the weekend.

items.title: 28 Things To Do In Chicago This Weekend: Chicago Fashion Week, Latino Dance Festival, Fall Fests
items.summary: The Chicago Marathon returns this weekend and the Jefferson Park and Luv City fall festivals are also on deck.

items.title: Chicago's 1st Battery-Powered Commuter Train Coming To Metra's Rock Island Beverly Line
items.summary: The "FLIRT" train, set to begin service in 2028, will be on display next week at the LaSalle Street Metra station.

items.title: How To Celebrate Indigenous Peoples' Day In Chicago
items.summary: We've compiled a list of events and Indigenous organizations you can support in Chicago and beyond.

items.title: Mayor Johnson counters Trump’s crime claims with data showing 30% drop in homicides
items.summary: President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that Chicago is experiencing an unprecedented violent crime wave and urged federal help. Mayor Brandon Johnson responded on CNN, citing Block Club data that the city has recorded 288 homicides this year, a 30 percent decline from the same time last year, and called the president out of touch. Johnson also demanded restoration of $800 million in federal funding for community violence intervention programs and the ATF budget.

items.title: Residents and City Council push back on $900 million Amtrak Bridgeport maintenance facility
items.summary: A proposed $900 million Amtrak maintenance facility in Bridgeport is facing opposition from local residents and City Council members, according to CBS 2’s Shardaa Gray. Critics are concerned about the project's impact on the neighborhood, though specific objections were not detailed in the report.

items.title: Mayor Johnson vows to tax the rich in 2027 budget to aid working families
items.summary: Ahead of the budget deadline, Mayor Brandon Johnson said his 2027 budget will level the playing field by taxing corporations that make more money while working people stand in lines for food, as reported by the Sun‑Times. The mayor framed the plan as a response to economic inequality in Chicago.

items.title: Sox playoffs pump up Bridgeport
items.summary: The energy outside Rate Field may not have propelled the Sox to an ALDS-clinching win yesterday, but it didn't stop fans from enjoying the moment. The Sox played their first home game of this year's playoffs, losing to the Guardians 9-3. Game 4 is at 7 tonight.

items.title: ATM stolen in crash-and-grab burglary at bar in Chicago's Little Italy
items.summary: Chicago police early Thursday were searching for the burglars behind a smash-and-grab at a bar in the Little Italy community.

items.title: Crash-and-grab burglars hit bar in Chicago's Little Italy
items.summary: Chicago police early Thursday were searching for the burglars behind a smash-and-grab at a bar in the Little Italy community.

items.title: White Sox Minority Owner's Firm Buys Another Property Near Proposed Ballpark In South Loop
items.summary: The $15 million purchase of The Maxwell shopping center by an affiliate of Justin Ishbia’s Shore Capital Partners adds to the footprint of his proposed Railyards development.

items.title: Block 37's New Owner Wants To Get Rid Of Old Mall Vibe'
items.summary: Edwards Realty Company plans to revamp the shopping center through retail, entertainment, culture, media, strategic partnerships and year-round programming.

items.title: Downtown Chicago's Block 37 mall sold for $30 million
items.summary: Downtown Chicago's Block 37 mall was sold to Edwards Realty Company this week for $30 million, the company announced Wednesday.

items.title: 5 Must-See Art Exhibits To Check Out In October
items.summary: This month’s selected exhibits draw inspiration from Greek myths, Black veterans and tattoo art.

items.title: Patty García endorsed by Track AIPAC and Justice Coalition Action PAC in IL‑04 race as Chuy Garcia retires
items.summary: Democratic nominee Patty García received endorsements from Track AIPAC and the Justice Coalition Action PAC for the Illinois House 4th District seat, which is being vacated by retiring incumbent Rep. Jesús “Chuy” García. The 4th District includes Chicago neighborhoods such as the West Loop, Near West Side, and Fulton Market, making the race directly relevant to 34th Ward residents. The endorsements signal strong support from progressive and pro‑Israel groups ahead of the upcoming primary.

items.title: Chicago Public Schools watchdog inquiry reopened, stirring controversy in school board president race
items.summary: A reopened Chicago Public Schools watchdog investigation is affecting a candidate for school board president after a woman alleged inappropriate behavior by candidate Hilario Domínguez. The allegation was reported by Block Club reporters Mila Koumpilova and Francia García Hernández and also covered by NBC 5’s Mary Ann Ahern. The controversy adds tension to the citywide school board president contest, which will impact policies affecting all Chicago public schools.

items.title: Illinois expands automatic sealing of criminal records under the Clean Slate Act
items.summary: The Clean Slate Act, amended this year, now moves Illinois toward automatically sealing eligible criminal records, with Cook County officials offering assistance to residents on Saturday. The change reduces waiting periods and eligibility restrictions, aiming to improve access to housing and employment for affected individuals. The statewide reform directly benefits Chicago residents, including those in the 34th Ward, by simplifying the record‑clearing process.

items.title: Trump wrong about Chicago crime
items.summary: Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images President Trump is again raising the prospect of federal intervention in Chicago, saying the city is suffering an "unprecedented" crime wave that's "getting worse by the day. " Trump's renewed focus on Chicago comes as the city is on pace to record even fewer homicides than last year, when killings fell to their lowest level in 60 years. Trump's words paint a bleak picture of violence.

items.title: Checking out the Chicago Brand Museum
items.summary: Take a look inside the Chicago Brand Museum in the South Loop.

items.title: Mayor Brandon Johnson marks completion of Missing Middle housing initiative in South Loop
items.summary: Mayor Brandon Johnson spoke at 1443 S. Trumbull Ave at 10 a.m. on Oct. 6, 2026 to announce the completion of the Missing Middle housing initiative, a city effort to increase affordable housing options in the South Loop area of the 34th Ward.

items.title: Federal judge blocks Illinois from enforcing parts of its sports wagering law against Kalshi
items.summary: U.S. District Judge Martha Pacold issued a 28‑page opinion on Friday ruling that Illinois likely cannot enforce key provisions of its 2019 sports wagering law against prediction market company Kalshi, Coinbase and related firms, citing federal Commodity Exchange Act jurisdiction; Attorney General Kwame Raoul’s office declined to comment.

items.title: Pritzker vs. Bailey
items.summary: The race for the governor's mansion is in its final month, and Democrats and Republicans are ramping up their attacks. The two are facing off for the second time as Gov. JB Pritzker seeks a third term that would further cement Democratic control in Springfield, while Republican Darren Bailey is promising a sharp change in direction.

items.title: Chicago Fashion Week Kicks Off Thursday With Runway Shows, Workshops, Parties And More
items.summary: From Hyde Park to Highland Park, there are more than 80 fashion events across the Chicago area. We've highlighted 15 of them here.

items.title: Tini Bar, With Room For Just 30 People, Goes Big On Retro Cocktails
items.summary: The 630-square-foot bar opening in November below LIA Tavern in River North takes inspiration from midcentury modern design and house parties of the 1950s through the ‘70s.

items.title: CTA Unveils 1950s Neon-Style Sign At Revamped Blue Line Stop
items.summary: The CTA recreated the sign used for the original Congress Line, which opened in 1958, at the newly reopened Loomis Street entrance to the Racine stop.

items.title: School Board president candidate Hilario Dominguez faces reopened investigation after rally with Mayor Brandon Johnson
items.summary: A Chicago School Board president candidate, Hilario Dominguez, appeared at a rally with Mayor Brandon Johnson in Pilsen on Oct. 3, one day after the Tribune reported that the Chicago Public Schools Office of Inspector General reopened an investigation into allegations from a 2017 summer youth program. The allegations involve inappropriate language and behavior toward a participant who was then 17, and the complainant, now 26, said she had not been interviewed. Dominguez left the event early and posted on social media that he believes in accountability and that previous investigations found the claims unfounded.

items.title: Former Mayor Rahm Emanuel discusses Democratic brand problem and potential 2028 presidential run on Meet the Press
items.summary: Former Chicago mayor Rahm Emanuel was interviewed on Meet the Press on Oct. 4, where he warned that Democrats have a brand problem and need to focus on solutions such as affordability and ethics. He dismissed efforts to impeach former President Trump as a food fight, criticized democratic socialists for defunding the police and open borders, and expressed support for Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El‑Sayed while hinting at a possible 2028 presidential bid.

items.title: How to vote in the midterm
items.summary: Stock: Getty Images Chicagoans can officially start casting ballots in the 2026 midterm election. You don't have to wait until Election Day on Nov. 3, but deadlines for registering, voting by mail and finding an early voting site are approaching.

items.title: Chicago City Council Ethics Committee to question World Business Chicago over mayor‑investment ads
items.summary: The City Council Committee on Ethics, chaired by Ald. Matt Martin, is scheduled to meet on October 1 to interrogate World Business Chicago about recent TV and streaming ads that promoted Mayor Brandon Johnson’s record on neighborhood investment. Council members have sent a letter demanding answers, and the outcome could affect the organization’s city funding. The meeting is part of heightened scrutiny ahead of the mayoral election.

items.title: City Council Ethics Committee Questions World Business Chicago Ads Ahead of Election
items.summary: The Chicago City Council Committee on Ethics, chaired by Ald. Matt Martin, met to question World Business Chicago about recent spending on local TV and streaming ads that touted Mayor Brandon Johnson’s record in neighborhood investment. The committee raised concerns that the ads, which had prompted a letter from council members, may involve city funding and could be at stake. The meeting also considered whether officials from World Business Chicago would attend to answer questions.

items.title: Design Museum of Chicago, a hidden gem in the Loop, showcases city's innovation
items.summary: A special museum tucked away in downtown Chicago is dedicated to design and how it shapes our lives.

items.title: A look inside the Design Museum of Chicago, a hidden gem in the Loop
items.summary: A special museum tucked away in downtown Chicago is dedicated to design and how it shapes our lives.

items.title: Gov. Pritzker meets NFL officials to discuss keeping Chicago Bears in Illinois
items.summary: On Oct. 1, 2026 Governor JB Pritzker met with NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell, Bears minority owner Pat Ryan, House Speaker Emanuel "Chris" Welch, Rep. Kam Buckner and Sen. Bill Cunningham in downtown Chicago. The meeting focused on a long‑term stadium solution for the Bears and the possibility of legislation that would preserve a path for either a Chicago or Arlington Heights site. Mayor Brandon Johnson was not present, and lawmakers will consider the issue during the November veto session.

items.title: Mayoral race remains fluid as John Kelly headlines City Club luncheon
items.summary: Businessman and lobbyist John Kelly addressed the City Club of Chicago on Oct. 1, 2026, emphasizing support for police and fixing potholes. Mayor Brandon Johnson used the same venue the day before to contrast his platform of higher corporate taxes and community investment with Kelly’s message. Kelly announced his endorsement of Victor Henderson for Chicago School Board president, while Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias reported a campaign war chest of more than $23 million.

items.title: Former Mayor Rahm Emanuel to speak at Obama Presidential Center on youth mentoring
items.summary: Rahm Emanuel will return to the Obama Presidential Center on Oct. 8, 2026 to discuss the power of youth mentoring as part of Youth Guidance’s Becoming A Man and Working on Womanhood programs. The appearance coincides with the rollout of his new book Do What Works, which includes a chapter on Chicago’s mentoring efforts. Emanuel previously highlighted the program to President Barack Obama in 2013, linking it to the My Brother’s Keeper initiative.

items.title: CTA Green and Pink Line service interruptions Oct. 13‑26 due to Lake Street Bridge replacement
items.summary: The Chicago Department of Transportation will replace the Lake Street Bridge, causing Green and Pink Line service to be interrupted between Clinton and Clark/Lake stations from 4 am on Oct. 13 to 4 am on Oct. 26. Green Line trains will run in two sections with free bus substitutions, and Pink Line riders will transfer to the Blue Line at Racine. Milwaukee Avenue will be closed from Canal to Fulton between Oct. 5 and Oct. 30, affecting West Loop commuters.

items.title: Dedicated northbound bus lane to be added on Michigan Avenue between Roosevelt and Wacker
items.summary: In partnership with the Chicago Department of Transportation, the CTA will install a 1.5‑mile dedicated bus lane on northbound Michigan Avenue from Roosevelt to Wacker. The lane will serve 21 bus routes that carry more than 7 million passengers annually and will include cameras that automatically ticket standing and moving violations as part of the Smart Streets Pilot. Installation will begin when weather permits.

items.title: City Council approves parking meter deal worth $139.2 million to taxpayers
items.summary: At Tuesday’s City Council meeting, members approved a change in control of Chicago’s parking meters that provides the city with $75 million upfront and a 5 percent share of calculated net income, valued at approximately $139.2 million to taxpayers. Council also passed an ordinance requiring a 60 percent vote before the city can take on additional debt, addressing a $2 billion debt load that threatens funding for parks, schools and police.

items.title: Black Briar Opens at 201 N. Morgan St in Fulton Market
items.summary: The West Central Association celebrated the grand opening of Black Briar, a new restaurant in Fulton Market, with a ribbon cutting ceremony. Led by Chef Jimmy Papadopoulos and co-owner Tim Anderson, the restaurant offers a menu featuring fresh seafood, house‑made pastas, steaks, and inventive cocktails. The opening marks a new addition to the vibrant dining scene in the West Loop area.

items.title: Chicago Marathon Street Closures Impact 29 Neighborhoods Including the 34th Ward
items.summary: The Chicago Marathon will run on Sunday, October 11, with extensive street closures and parking restrictions affecting the 34th Ward. Towing will begin at 1:00 AM, and streets along the route will close to traffic as early as 6:00 AM, reopening around 4:00 PM. The route change for miles 1–2 in the Loop will have traffic travel south on Dearborn St. instead of State St. Residents should consult the Street Closure Brochure for exact times.

items.title: Great Chicago Bed Race Returns Sunday, October 4 at Midwest Coast Brewing Co.
items.summary: The 2nd Annual Great Chicago Bed Race will take place on Sunday, October 4, at Midwest Coast Brewing Co. Teams of five will race twin XL mattresses down Walnut Street to raise funds for the Chicago Furniture Bank. The event aims to furnish 4,004 homes for families transitioning out of homelessness.

items.title: Chicago Brand Museum In The South Loop Is A Trip Down Memory Lane
items.summary: The vintage labels, familiar products and forgotten designs on display reveal how the brands of the past can spark memories.

items.title: Early voting for the November 3 election is open at two downtown sites
items.summary: Early voting for the November 3 general election is now underway at 137 S. State St. and 69 W. Washington St. Residents can also register to vote or update their registration at both sites. The Chicago Board of Elections is also recruiting poll workers, including bilingual judges who speak Spanish, Chinese, Hindi, Polish, Korean, and Tagalog.

items.title: Green and Pink Line service cut between Clinton and Clark/Lake Oct. 13-26 for Lake Street Bridge work
items.summary: From 4 a.m. October 13 to 4 a.m. October 26, Green and Pink Line trains will not run between Clinton and Clark/Lake while CDOT replaces the Lake Street Bridge, with free shuttle buses covering the gap. Pink Line trains will route to the Blue Line's Racine station for downtown service. Separately, Milwaukee Avenue will be closed from Canal to Fulton from October 5 to October 30.

items.title: Sheridan Park Pumpkin Patch returns Saturday, Oct. 3
items.summary: The annual Sheridan Park Pumpkin Patch runs Saturday, October 3, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Sheridan Park, 910 S. Aberdeen St. The free family event, co-hosted with the Chicago Park District, includes a pumpkin patch, petting zoo, and crafts.

items.title: Columbus Day Parade brings Loop street closures Monday, Oct. 12
items.summary: The Columbus Day Parade steps off at noon on Monday, October 12, from Dearborn and Lake and heads south to Jackson. No-parking restrictions start at 7 a.m. on Wacker (Wabash to Franklin), Dearborn (Wacker to Van Buren), and Van Buren (State to Franklin), with east-west streets crossing Dearborn closing at 11 a.m. All streets are expected to reopen by 3 p.m.

items.title: Gov. Pritzker meets NFL officials to keep Chicago Bears in Illinois
items.summary: On Oct. 1, 2026 Governor JB Pritzker met with NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell, Bears minority owner Pat Ryan, House Speaker Emanuel "Chris" Welch, Rep. Kam Buckner and Sen. Bill Cunningham in downtown Chicago. The meeting focused on keeping the Bears in Illinois and finding a long‑term stadium solution as Indiana officials continue courting the team. The NFL said it appreciated the opportunity and called timely action essential for the club and its fans.

items.title: Mayor Brandon Johnson attends United Yards 1A ribbon‑cutting
items.summary: Mayor Brandon Johnson gave remarks at the United Yards 1A ribbon‑cutting at 4706 S. Justine St. on Oct. 1, 2026.

items.title: Evanston's new Ryan Field
items.summary: An aerial view of the new Ryan Field in Evanston from early September. Courtesy of Central Street Consortium Northwestern football returns home tonight, unveiling its $870 million Ryan Field nearly three years after the old stadium was demolished. The debut is the first real-world test of the deal Northwestern and Evanston hammered out after a bruising fight over concerts, noise, traffic and the stadium's impact.

items.title: Black Briar opens in Fulton Market
items.summary: Black Briar opened at 201 N. Morgan St. in Fulton Market, with chef Jimmy Papadopoulos and co‑owner Tim Anderson leading the new restaurant. The ribbon‑cutting ceremony was held recently, and the menu features fresh seafood, house‑made pastas, steaks, inventive cocktails and an extensive wine list. The venue adds to Fulton Market’s vibrant dining scene.

items.title: Triskele Health to open large West Loop facility
items.summary: Triskele Health announced a new 10,000‑square‑foot facility at 15 S. Aberdeen Street in the West Loop. The multidisciplinary practice will offer physical therapy, nutrition, strength and conditioning, and mental performance services, integrating wearable technology for data‑driven care. The opening expands health‑and‑wellness options for West Loop residents and businesses.

items.title: Chicago Marathon street closures affect the Loop
items.summary: The Chicago Marathon on Sunday, October 11 will close streets in the Loop and surrounding neighborhoods, with no parking permitted along the course starting at 1:00 AM. Neighborhood streets will close to traffic as early as 6:00 AM and reopen around 4:00 PM, and the route’s first two miles will travel south on Dearborn St. instead of State St. Residents should review the street‑closure brochure for exact times and restrictions.

items.title: Search Is On For Chicago's Official Christmas Tree
items.summary: Chicagoans can submit nominations online through Oct. 23. Norway spruce and fir trees and trees within 15 miles of the city are preferred.

items.title: City Council Ethics Committee to question World Business Chicago over mayor‑investment ads
items.summary: The Chicago City Council Committee on Ethics, chaired by Alderman Matt Martin, scheduled a meeting today to interrogate World Business Chicago about recent TV and streaming ads that highlighted Mayor Brandon Johnson’s neighborhood investment record. Council members have sent a letter demanding answers, and the organization’s city funding could be jeopardized pending the outcome.

items.title: Michael and Cari Sacks give $600,000 to Michael Reese Health Trust for women’s abortion access
items.summary: Philanthropists Michael and Cari Sacks contributed $600,000 to the Michael Reese Health Trust, earmarked to support its women’s abortion access fund, according to a report by Crain’s.

items.title: Chicago Park District’s first town hall focuses on speed and enforcement of motorized devices
items.summary: At the Chicago Park District’s inaugural town hall on motorized devices, speed limits and enforcement emerged as the primary concerns among attendees, as reported by WTTW’s Patty Wetli.

items.title: Randolph Row Holiday Stroll scheduled for Dec 10 in West Loop
items.summary: The West Loop Community Organization announced its annual Randolph Row Holiday Stroll will take place on December 10, inviting shoppers to participating West Loop stores that will offer special deals and steals throughout the day. The event is promoted as a family-friendly way to celebrate the holiday season and businesses can sign up via a participation form.

items.title: Chicago Police Department holds Community Conversations on Oct 1 and Oct 22
items.summary: The CPD will host round-table Community Conversations on October 1 and October 22, giving West Loop residents a chance to speak directly with officers who patrol the neighborhood and discuss public safety concerns. The meetings are open to anyone who wants to voice their opinions and learn about police initiatives.

items.title: 3rd Annual Trunk or Treat Halloween event set for Oct 18
items.summary: The 012th District and community partners will organize the third annual Trunk or Treat on October 18, offering a family-friendly afternoon of Halloween festivities in the West Loop. Attendees can enjoy decorated car trunks, candy, and activities in a safe neighborhood setting.

items.title: CTA installing dedicated bus lane on Michigan Avenue in the Loop
items.summary: CTA bus riders could soon get a faster trip through downtown Chicago.

items.title: You Can Tour The Uptown Theatre As Part Of Open House Chicago This Year
items.summary: Other new sites announced Thursday in advance of the Oct. 17-18 event include the Monadnock Building and the new Chicago Architecture Center hub at the Marquette Building.

items.title: Mayor Brandon Johnson to speak at Parkside ribbon‑cutting on West Loop
items.summary: Mayor Brandon Johnson will be at 520 W Hobbie St at 9 a.m. on October 1 to give remarks at the Parkside ribbon‑cutting ceremony. The event is in the West Loop, part of the 34th Ward, and highlights a new community space opening in the neighborhood.

items.title: City Council Committee on Ethics to question World Business Chicago over mayor‑investment ads
items.summary: The Chicago City Council Committee on Ethics, chaired by Ald. Matt Martin, is meeting today to interrogate World Business Chicago about recent TV and streaming ads that promoted Mayor Brandon Johnson’s neighborhood‑investment record. Council members have sent a letter demanding answers on the ad buys ahead of the mayoral election, and the organization’s city funding could be at risk.

items.title: Chicago Park District holds first town hall on motorized devices
items.summary: The Chicago Park District hosted its inaugural town hall focused on motorized devices, where speed and enforcement emerged as the top concerns among attendees. The discussion was reported by WTTW’s Patty Wetli.

items.title: Sox move on, Cubs go home
items.summary: Randal Grichuk celebrates with teammates after the White Sox defeated the Houston Astros yesterday. Connor Jalbert/MLB Photos via Getty Images The White Sox wasted little time punching their ticket to the divisional round with back-to-back wins over the Houston Astros, while the Cubs' season sputtered to an end with a quick exit in San Diego. Dreams of a crosstown World Series are dashed.

items.title: Dedicated Bus Lane Coming To Michigan Avenue Downtown
items.summary: The nearly 1.5-mile northbound lane will run from Roosevelt Road to Wacker Drive and serve 21 CTA routes used by thousands of riders each day.

items.title: 24 Things To Do In Chicago This Weekend: Block Club Chicago Block Party And More
items.summary: Block Club’s third annual Block Party is back at Half Acre Beer Co. You can also check out the Latina Comedy Festival, Apple Fest and Bears watch parties.

items.title: R B Artist Manasseh, A South Side Native, Showcases Local Collaborations On New Album
items.summary: The musician and vocal coach released his fifth album "R Beyond" last month. He plays Pitch Pour Supper Club on the West Side Friday.

items.title: Chicago to install dedicated bus lane on northbound Michigan Avenue downtown
items.summary: Seeking to reduce delays for CTA riders in downtown Chicago, officials plan to install a new dedicated bus lane on Michigan Avenue.

items.title: Chicago Youth Stored Their Pandemic Lives In Time Capsules. Now, You Can Look Inside
items.summary: The “Look Back to Go Forward” exhibit displays artifacts kids and teens put in time capsules in 2021 and gives visitors a chance to reflect on their own pandemic experiences.

items.title: City transfers 2008 parking meter lease to Stonepeak Partners for $2.53 billion
items.summary: The Chicago City Council voted 46‑3 to approve the sale of the remaining years of the 2008 parking meter lease to New York‑based Stonepeak Partners for roughly $2.53 billion. Chicago will receive an upfront payment of $75 million, a 5 percent share of future net revenues, and a 2 percent right to any future resale price. Officials say the funds and revenue stream will be directed toward reducing the city’s pension obligations, and the deal gives the city more flexibility to shut down meters for special events without paying compensation.

items.title: City Council adopts 30‑vote threshold for new debt proposals
items.summary: In a move that defies the mayor’s position, the Chicago City Council approved a rule requiring a supermajority of 30 votes to approve any new municipal debt. The change aims to tighten fiscal oversight and limit the administration’s ability to incur additional borrowing without broad council support.

items.title: After School Matters fundraiser raises nearly $2.7 million
items.summary: The After School Matters fundraiser attracted a crowd of 500, including civic leader Nora Daley and Cook County Commissioner John Daley, and generated almost $2.7 million for the organization’s youth programs.

items.title: United CEO aims high
items.summary: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby wants the airline's home base to be the best in the world. In a new interview with the "Office Hours: Business Edition" podcast, Kirby lays out an ambitious vision: Make O'Hare the world's No. Kirby's vision could supercharge Chicago's status as a global aviation hub - or put even more pressure on an air traffic control system already struggling to keep up.

items.title: Culver’s Coming To Former Aurelio's Spot In South Loop
items.summary: The Wisconsin-based fast-food chain is planning to open at 1212 S. Michigan Ave., in the former Aurelio’s Pizza space.

items.title: 13 Things To Do Outside In Chicago This October
items.summary: Grab a pumpkin, watch a spooky movie or enjoy a witchy bike ride in and around Chicago this month.

items.title: Chicago police investigating string of 40 car burglaries in Bronezville and South Loop
items.summary: Chicago police need help to find a group of thieves who have broken into at least 40 cars in the last few weeks on the Near South Side.

items.title: City Council Budget Accountability Coalition urges mayor to avoid property tax hike in 2027 budget
items.summary: A bloc of 29 aldermen, calling themselves the City Council Budget Accountability Coalition, sent Mayor Brandon Johnson a letter demanding no property tax increase, no head tax, and no counting of unapproved Springfield money in the 2027 budget. The aldermen cite an $882.4 million budget gap and reference a $3 million Ernst & Young efficiency review that identified over $1 billion in potential savings. items.summary: The West Loop Historic Plaques Project will add four new plaques in summer 2026, marking a UIC classroom, a condominium building, and two parks, bringing the total to nineteen historic designations, four historic plaques, and one Chicago Landmark plaque in the neighborhood.

items.title: West Loop Green City Market returns for Saturday season
items.summary: The West Loop Green City Market operates Saturdays from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. at 900 W. Monroe, running May through November and featuring dozens of local farmers and food producers; the market will be closed on September 19 due to weather.

items.title: Reserv Owner Says He's Closing South Loop Restaurant After Months Of Neighbor Complaints
items.summary: The city issued a cease-and-desist notice after a fight prompted a large police response in August. Neighbors had previously levied frequent noise complaints.

items.title: State’s Attorney Agrees To Meet With Latino Leaders Demanding She Investigate ICE
items.summary: Immigration advocates have pressed Cook County State’s Attorney Eileen O’Neill Burke to probe the actions of federal immigration agents during Operation Midway Blitz.
